digest.component_or_area: MCP server error surface and library error classification
propositions: MCP tool failures currently surface as unstructured prose or ad-hoc partial shapes, while the CLI emits a structured error_envelope discriminator; MCP must emit the same discriminator from a single shared vocabulary

The error code vocabulary is scattered across CLI call sites (12 distinct emitters) and does not exist centrally; a single error_code_for(exc)->str classifier and KNOWN_ERROR_CODES frozenset must be added to _errors.py as the source of truth

The library interface currently exposes no machine error code, so a three-way cross-interface test (library / CLI / MCP) has no library-side value to compare; error_code_for must be re-exported as rebar.error_code_for

MCP's two soft-error returns (_mcp_reads explain_criterion and _mcp_llm) emit divergent ad-hoc shapes with no vocabulary code; they must gain a code (drawn from KNOWN_ERROR_CODES) while preserving existing agent-branching fields (kind, resolution_class, retryable, diagnostic)

Exception-raised MCP failures must be caught and wrapped in McpEnvelopeError (carrying a structured .envelope dict) before FastMCP's ToolError reaches the wire, so consumers can read the code off __cause__.envelope without fragile prefix-stripping

TicketNotFoundError must be added as a subclass of ReadError, raised only at the genuine not-found sites (reads.py:310/313) with identical message, so the message-keyed CLI classifier stays byte-unchanged and AC6 (CLI regression) holds
